title: Compact span sink and deferred metric aggregation to reduce runtime telemetry overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce CPU and allocation overhead from the agent-side telemetry path by introducing a compact zero-copy span sink, reordering OTEL filter chain, and implementing a deferred metric aggregator with batched flushes. Goal: lower p99 CPU on runtime-serving processes by 25% under steady-state load and reduce span export-related allocations by ~60%.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end latency impact of tracing path under 95th percentile should be <2ms added per request on average (measured on runtime-1.20 staging).
Span serializer allocations reduced by at least 50% compared to baseline (compare flamegraphs + benchmark traces).
Deferred metric aggregator reduces cardinality churn to keep metric ingestion rate within current quota for medium workloads (validated with synthetic load test).
No user-visible loss of critical spans or metrics in canary at 10% with fallback enabled; dropped_spans <= 0.1% in canary window.
Feature gate + rollout controls present and documented; rollback path validated with an emergency feature toggle.
technical_notes: Introduce a compact SpanSink that writes spans into a pre-allocated byte slab using a zero-copy encoding (tag index + varint lengths) to minimize per-span heap allocations.
Swap the current OTEL processor ordering: move sampling and tag-normalization earlier to avoid heavy tag processing for dropped spans.
DeferredMetricAggregator: collect gauge/counter updates in-thread into a small ring buffer and flush to the exporter on a coalesced interval (configurable, default 5s) or when thresholds are hit.
Keep OTLP exporter batching but reduce buffer growth by bounding in-flight batches and exposing backpressure metrics (export_queue_length, export_backpressure_events).
Use flatbuffers-lite for span serialization in the sink to allow shared memory between runtime and exporter where possible (mmap for dedicated nodes).
Minimize locks: use per-worker slab pools + single-writer ring for cross-thread handoff. Fall back to lockless CAS where supported to avoid contention at high qps.
Replace expensive JSON log struct allocations in the telemetry path with a compact binary journal writer; retain human-readable logs in a parallel slow-path only for debug mode.
implementation_tasks: Create span_slab allocator and zero-copy SpanSink API (ENG-86142-1).
Implement sampling reordering in OTEL processor chain and add unit tests (ENG-86142-2).
Build DeferredMetricAggregator with bounded ring buffer and flush logic, add metrics for buffer fullness and flush latency (ENG-86142-3).
Integrate compact sink with OTLP exporter and add mmap-backed path for Dedicated nodes (ENG-86142-4).
Add feature flag / runtime config: telemetry.compact_sink_enabled (default off).
Benchmarks: write microbench harness for span serialization, integration load test against staging (100k rps synthetic trace traffic).
Docs: update Console instrumentation docs and runtime upgrade notes with new config knobs and troubleshooting steps.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag; land in runtime-1.21 branch with e2e tests in CI.
Canary 1% of serving fleet for 24h: monitor CPU, memory, export queues, and dropped_spans.
If stable, increase to 10% for 48h and run synthetic 100k rps trace test against canary nodes.
Promote to 50% with autoscaling observing; keep fallback toggle ready for immediate rollback.
Full rollout after 7 days of healthy telemetry signals and no regressions in latency or user-reported traces.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard: CompactSink / DeferredMetrics health (span_serialize_latency, span_alloc_bytes, export_queue_length, deferred_metric_flush_time).
Alert: export_queue_length > 1000 for 2m => P1 on-call (possible exporter backpressure).
Alert: dropped_spans rate > 0.5% for 5m in canary cohort => rollback feature flag immediately.
Add trace comparison job: nightly job to diff sample traces and ensure key span annotations preserved.
SLO: maintain span export success rate >= 99.9% across rollout windows.
